units.title: Recycling round: missed again, week three.
units.author: sb_bins
units.text: Rope Walk blue bins were not emptied this morning, for the third week running. The council newsletter of last week states, and I quote, 'all rounds are operating to the published schedule'. They are not. I rang the council line at 7:02 and pressed 3, then 1, then 4, and was told my call was important. It was, and it still is. Bernard (Rope Walk)

units.author: dc_3_wendell
units.text: Bernard, same story in Weyhaven, different council, same phone menu. Our general waste on the eighth floor sat there all Tuesday. I have started writing down every missed collection in a notebook with the time and the registration of the lorry. If yours is anything like ours, the newsletter is written by people who have never seen a bin.

units.title: Carrow Point readings, day 10.
units.author: wx_carrowpoint
units.text: Morning readings from the back garden station: pressure 1009 hPa and falling slowly, wind SW 4 m/s gusting 9, dew point 8.1 C against air 9.0 C, so damp but not fog. Visibility a disappointing 4 km in drizzle. Rain gauge 3.2 mm overnight. The fog week is properly over, I'm sorry to report. Textbook advection fog while it lasted. Now just a grey lid.

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Grey lid's right. Couldn't see the Holm from the harbour wall this morning, only the top of the ridge now and then. Swell from the southwest picking up by the afternoon. Aye, I'll take drizzle over fog any day.

units.title: Kittering Holm: discussion thread, week two.
units.author: sb_mod
units.text: Good morning. As the previous Holm thread had grown to an unreadable length, I have closed it and opened this one. A reminder of the house rules for this subject. Please give a source for any factual claim. Please do not post speculation about named individuals, including the crew working there. The altered planning screenshot removed last week is not to be reposted in any form. Thank you. Pell (Admin).

units.author: skeptic_planner
units.text: For anyone arriving new, the actual record. Application ADC/VC/0311, 'total vegetation clearance, Kittering Holm', applicant an agent for Ardent Vale Holdings, determined under delegated powers. Conditions: no works within 10 m of mean high water; a breeding bird check if works run past March; the landing stage to be left in place. Nothing about any future use. The word 'evacuation' appears nowhere in the file.

units.author: truthwatch_gil
units.text: Just asking questions here but nobody has explained why a quiet billionaire holding company needs EVERY tree gone in thirty days. Not some. All. Ask yourself what you'd want if you needed somewhere with clear sightlines. And for the record I did not make that screenshot, it was sent to me by someone who works near the council, and I shared it in good faith. Do your research.

units.author: skeptic_planner
units.text: Gil, the screenshot used a typeface the council has not used since its website changed two years ago, and the inserted line was in a different font size from the rest of the notice. Whoever sent it to you, it was altered. As for 'every tree': total clearance is common before a site is levelled, replanted or sold on. The scale is unusual. The wording isn't.

units.title: New history society pages: the Gilliver lamp, and more to come.
units.author: hist_wiki_marsh
units.text: Several people on the Holm thread have asked about Gilliver's window lamps, so the Society has finished and published its page on the custom, drawing on the oral history recordings and our parish notes. In short: a lamp kept lit in a front window overnight, recorded since at least the 1880s, explained by those who keep it as a courtesy. Further pages on the curing station and the timber camp will follow this week.

units.title: Still no Pebble (grey cat, one white sock).
units.author: sb_lostcat
units.text: Day eight without Pebble. Grey, short hair, one white sock on the front left paw, green collar with a bell she hates. I've walked every alley behind the market twice tonight with a torch and a box of treats. Thank you Mrs Ilse at number 9 for checking her garage, and the boys at the chippy for the poster. If anyone hears a bell, please, please shout.

units.author: sb_mod
units.text: Moved to Lost & Found again, where it will be seen by the right people. I hope Pebble turns up soon. A practical suggestion: neighbours with sheds and outbuildings might check them, as cats often get shut in by accident and go quiet after a few days. Pell (Admin).

units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: Not much help from Tollinby but: 1. put her litter tray outside your door, they can smell it from a long way off; 2. shake the treat box at the same time every night; 3. ask the bin men, they see everything at 6am. My middle one has drawn a poster of Pebble with six legs, which I'm not putting up, but the thought is there.

units.title: Freezer after the Brackwater power cut: what's safe?
units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: We're on the edge of the Brackwater area and lost power from about 8pm to just after 2am. Questions: 1. the chest freezer was shut the whole time, is everything ok or do I bin the fish fingers? 2. will Sound Power pay for anything that's spoiled? 3. does anyone know if the primary school at Brackwater is open today, the website just says 'check back'.

units.author: sb_bins
units.text: A full chest freezer kept shut will hold for a day or more. Six hours is nothing. As for compensation, the co-op's own leaflet, which I have here, says claims are considered for outages over 12 hours. You are four hours short, I'm afraid. Bernard (Rope Walk)

units.author: lineman_garvey
units.text: Your freezer's fine, keep the lid shut a bit longer and it'll be like nothing happened. The school opened at ten, my neighbour's kids went. For anyone wondering, it was a failed insulator at the substation, old age, replaced this morning. Nothing to do with the Holm, nothing to do with anyone stealing power, I've heard both today.

units.author: propwatch_ledger
units.text: Findings, continued from last week. 1. The intermediary that bought the Holm, Hesketh Lane Nominees, transferred it to Ardent Vale nine months after purchase. 2. Hesketh Lane's registered office is an accountancy firm in Halvard. 3. Its two directors are also directors of eleven other nominee companies. I make no claim about what this means beyond the fact that it was done carefully. I'll keep digging.

units.author: skeptic_ferrous
units.text: Good, careful work, ledger. I'd ask the usual question: what would we expect to see if this were simply land speculation? A nominee purchase to keep the price down, a transfer to the real owner, then clearance to make the land easier to value or sell. That's exactly what you've found. It doesn't rule out anything stranger. It just doesn't need it.

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: From the water: the boat goes out every few days with the crew's supplies, and there's a lot of saw noise when the wind's right. You can see the top of the ridge thinning from my line. Nothing strange, just men working hard. Nobody I know fishes close in after dark, mind. Not because of anything.

units.title: 07:20 from Lisle: late again, and the coffee machine.
units.author: sb_commuter_lisle
units.text: The 07:20 from Lisle left at 07:34 this morning, which Sound Lines will no doubt describe as 'minor disruption due to visibility'. The visibility was fine. The coffee machine in the saloon has also been broken since the fog, which is the real crisis. Arrived at my desk at 08:41 with no coffee. That's three late mornings out of five this week.

units.author: retired_teacher
units.text: Ewan, I believe the delay was caused by a lorry that could not be persuaded up the ramp at Lisle; I watched from my window with some amusement. I would also gently point out that 'three late mornings out of five this week' would be clearer as 'three late mornings this week'. I hope the coffee machine is repaired soon. Mrs Hale

units.author: sb_commuter_lisle
units.text: Thank you, Mrs Hale, on both counts. The lorry explains the 14 minutes. It doesn't explain the coffee. The 17:45 home was on time, for once, so I'll stop complaining for one evening. Possibly two.

units.title: Slipway sightings (moved from Harbour Chat, at their request).
units.author: sb_mod
units.text: Opened as a home for the slipway discussion that Harbour Chat would rather not host. The ferry crew report from Gilliver last week is already well known. Please keep in mind that the people who reported it are working staff who live locally. Jokes are permitted. Unkindness is not. Pell (Admin).

units.author: skeptic_brisk
units.text: Bloke stands on a slipway in fog. Ferry crew get spooked. That's it, that's the whole story. Fishermen stand on slipways, it's practically their job. Lads, it's a man in a coat.

units.author: sb_lostcat
units.text: Thank you so much, TollinbyMum, I've put the litter tray out (my neighbour across the road thinks I've gone mad) and I'll shake the treats at nine every night. Please tell your middle one six legs is fine, Pebble would probably like the extra ones for climbing fences. Thank you Pell for moving it. I'll ask the bin men tomorrow.

units.author: hollow_signal
units.text: Clear sightlines... you're closer than you think, Gil. I won't say how I know, but the people who buy islands like that don't buy them for the view. Watch what happens when the last trees come down. Watch who arrives. I've said too much already...

units.author: skeptic_orla
units.text: Source? No, really, source. You've 'said too much' in eleven threads now and never once said anything. For the record, the overnight show has had four callers this week about the Holm: one thinks it's a hotel, one a prison, one a 'bunker for the rich' and one just wanted to know if the saws will be quiet by Christmas. That last one is the only one with a point.

units.author: sb_mod
units.text: Bernard, I have forwarded your post to my former colleagues in Waste Services, with a polite note. I understand a round has been short of a driver since the end of last month and Rope Walk has been the casualty. I make no promises. Pell (Admin).

units.title: Carrow Point readings, day 11.
units.author: wx_carrowpoint
units.text: Day 11: pressure 1006 hPa, still drifting down. Wind S 6 m/s gusting 12. Air 10.4 C, dew point 9.7 C, light rain, visibility 6 km. Interesting high cloud streaks to the southwest at dawn, mares' tails as my grandmother called them, which tend to arrive ahead of something more organised. I'll be watching the barometer with more interest than is healthy.

units.author: lineman_tess
units.text: Following this closely from the co-op side. Garvey says when Carrow Point gets excited about clouds we should check the van's chains are in the back. Any idea yet whether it's the weekend or early next week?

units.author: wx_carrowpoint
units.text: Tess, my own guess, and it's only that, is a deepening low arriving late on day 13 or during day 14, with the strongest winds overnight. The Met Office will say it properly. Tell Garvey the chains are a good idea and so is a thermos.

units.title: The 'quarantine station' on the Holm: a correction.
units.author: retired_teacher
units.text: I have seen it said three times this week, on this board and in the Courier's letters, that there was once a 'quarantine station' on Kittering Holm. There was not. There was a fish-curing station, on the north shore, where herring were salted and smoked for the mainland market. I taught at Lisle school for thirty-four years and my pupils researched it more than once. Mrs Hale

units.author: hist_wiki_marsh
units.text: Mrs Hale is quite right, as she generally was when I sat in her classroom. The Society's new page on the curing station sets out what we hold: a lease from the 1880s, a few wage notes, and later fishermen's memories. The 'quarantine' version seems to start with a newspaper rumour early last century, which was corrected at the time. Citation needed on exactly when; I am still looking.

units.author: truthwatch_gil
units.text: Funny how the 'correction' always comes from the same few people. A quarantine station would be EXACTLY the kind of place you'd want to hide later and call something else. I'm not saying it was, I'm saying the official version is always the boring one. Ask why the curing station was abandoned. Just asking.

units.author: skeptic_planner
units.text: It was abandoned because the herring went. Fish-curing stations up and down the Sound closed in the same twenty years, when the shoals moved and the railway made it cheaper to ship fresh. The boring version is boring because it happened everywhere. Gil, that is a source-free post on a board that asks for sources.

units.author: gilliver_lamp
units.text: My grandmotther worked at the curing station as a girl, gutting, and she said it stank of smoke so you could smell it from Gilliver on an east wind. Nobody was ever sick there that I heard of, only cold. She kept the lamp lit too, but that is a different matter. Thank you Mrs Hale for putting it right.

units.author: retired_teacher
units.text: Thank you, Maud. Your grandmother's memory of the smell is exactly the sort of evidence that my pupils used to collect, and much more convincing than any rumour. I may still have one of the class projects in a box in the spare room. I shall look this week, if my knees allow the ladder.

units.author: skeptic_brisk
units.text: 'Watch who arrives.' Mate, a supply boat arrives. With sandwiches. Some rich bloke is clearing his island so he can sell it to a richer bloke. Every week there's a new theory: hotel, bunker, data centre, landing strip for aliens. It's trees. Grow up.

units.author: skeptic_planner
units.text: Taking the theories in turn, since they keep coming. Data centre: there's no grid connection or cable landing application, and the Holm has no supply. Hotel: no change-of-use application, and you'd need one. Landing strip: none of the application drawings shows levelling. None of that proves what it's for. It does tell you what nobody has applied for yet.

units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: Genuine question from someone with three children who have heard all of this at school: is there any danger to anyone on the mainland from what's happening on the Holm? My eldest came home saying they're 'building a shelter for when it happens'. When what happens, I asked. He didn't know. Nor do I.

units.author: sb_mod
units.text: TollinbyMum, to the best of anyone's knowledge on this board, no. It is a large tree-clearing contract on an uninhabited island, approved in the normal way. The 'shelter' story appears to be playground embroidery of things written here, which is one reason I ask for sources. Pell (Admin).

units.author: truthwatch_gil
units.text: 'To the best of anyone's knowledge.' Exactly. Nobody KNOWS. The council approved it under delegated powers, which means no committee, no vote, no questions. A private refuge for the rich, on an island you can watch from three villages, cleared so nothing can come at it unseen. I'm going to put this in my mailing list tonight, people deserve to know what questions aren't being asked.

units.author: sb_mod
units.text: Gil, delegated powers is how most applications are decided, including the extension to your own garage four years ago, which I remember because I processed it. You may ask questions. Please present them as questions, and not as facts with a question mark on the end. Pell (Admin).

units.title: Brackwater junction temporary lights: still red.
units.author: sb_roadworks
units.text: Brackwater jct lights still stuck on red heading north, 05:50 this morning. Sat through two full cycles before the green came on for about four seconds, enough for one van and a bicycle. The roadworks sign says 'completion expected end of month'. Which month, it doesn't say. Diversion via the reservoir road is quicker if you don't mind potholes the size of a bath.

units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: The school bus has been ten minutes late every morning since those lights went in and the driver told the kids it's 'the worst junction in the Sound'. Two of them now say it at home. Is there anyone at the council we can actually email, not the form that never replies?

units.author: sb_roadworks
units.text: Highways inbox on the council site, the one under 'Report a problem', then 'Temporary signals'. They do reply, in about a fortnight, saying the contractor is aware. Evening run: lights changed properly at 18:05, so I'm guessing they work fine when nobody needs them. There was a van parked up in the lay-by on the reservoir side again, same as last week, no lights on.

units.author: harbourmaster_quill
units.text: Posted here as well, for those who don't read Harbour Chat. Under Harbour Byelaw 14, the slipways at Gilliver and Lisle are closed to pedestrians from sunset to sunrise except for launching or recovering boats. A chain will be across the Gilliver slip at night from this evening. This is a safety measure. Please report anyone on a slip after dark to the harbour office. Thank you. M. Quill, Harbourmaster.

units.author: sb_commuter_lisle
units.text: So it's reached byelaws. Lisle is now talking about nothing else on the 17:45, according to the woman behind me who told the whole saloon. Ada from the pier is apparently the second witness. She's a sensible woman. I'd still bet on an angler who didn't fancy explaining himself to a ferry with a loud-hailer.

units.author: lisle_crew_ada
units.text: Ewan, ha, I'd bet on that too, honestly... I'd quite like to lose that bet to an angler. I don't want to be 'the second witness', I just do the pier lights. I've told the harbour office and the skipper and that's me done. If anyone did go fishing off the Lisle slip the other night, please just say, nobody's cross.

units.author: gilliver_teen
units.text: a chain lol. the tall slipway man is going to step over it. he is TALL. honestly though who even goes on the slip at night its freezing and it smells of weed. ferry people need to get out more. or less. one of those

units.author: skeptic_orla
units.text: Producer's note from the overnight show: we've had three callers this week who 'heard from a friend on the ferry' about the slipway man, and by the third call he was seven feet tall and had been seen on both slips the same night. Two sightings, one story, and it grows every time it's told. That's how this always goes.

units.author: sb_lostcat
units.text: Day nine. The bin men were lovely and said they'd look but hadn't seen a grey cat, only foxes and 'a very fat ginger one'. I shook the treats at nine. Nothing. Pell, I'll do the sheds tomorrow, starting with the allotments behind Tanner Street. Thank you everyone who's shared the poster. I'm trying not to read the sad stories about cats that never came back.

units.author: gilliver_lamp
units.text: Dear, my mother's cat was gone eleven days once and came home thin and cross and lived to be nineteen. Don't read the sad ones. Keep shaking the treats. Cats are very good at being shut in places and very bad at telling anyone.

units.title: Brackwater estate: night access reminder.
units.author: brackwater_keeper
units.text: Since the woods have got popular on the internet. The Brackwater estate woods and reservoir paths are closed from dusk to dawn. The car park gate is locked at 18:00 in winter. There are deep drainage cuts off the east path that you won't see in the dark, and the reservoir edge is steep. I'm not interested in your recordings or your streams. I'm interested in not pulling anyone out of a ditch.

units.author: dunlin_rec
units.text: Understood, and fair. For what it's worth, I've been parking on the reservoir road rather than in the estate car park and keeping to the path, but I take the point about the ditches. I'll keep future sessions to the public footpath on the west side where I can. Thanks for the warning, genuinely.

units.author: nightscream_vlog
units.text: public footpaths are public guys, no gamekeeper can stop you walking on them. just saying. stream still happening

units.author: lh_insomniac_tollinby
units.text: TollinbyMum, for whatever comfort it is from a man awake at three: every generation in the Sound has had an island story. When I was small it was that the Holm had wolves. Before that, my grandfather said, it was smugglers. The children are doing what children have always done with an island they can see and can't visit. It doesn't make it true. It doesn't make them wrong to wonder.

units.author: sb_bins
units.text: Thank you, Pell. A van, not a lorry, came to Rope Walk at 6:48 this morning and took the blue bins from numbers 1 to 22. Numbers 23 to 40 remain full. The driver told me he 'only had the one list'. I have asked for a copy of the other list. Partial victory. The newsletter remains incorrect. Bernard (Rope Walk)

units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: Bernard, you are a hero of the people. Can you come and do Tollinby next? Our glass hasn't been collected since the half-term and my recycling box now has its own ecosystem.

units.title: Carrow Point readings, day 12.
units.author: wx_carrowpoint
units.text: Day 12: pressure 1001 hPa, the steepest fall this month. Wind S 8 m/s gusting 15. Air 11.2 C, very mild, dew point 10.8 C. Showers through the night, 6.4 mm. Visibility good between them, 15 km, Lisle clear and the Holm ridge sharp. The barograph trace looks like a ski jump. I'll put the garden chairs in the shed today, which is my version of a weather warning.

units.author: sb_commuter_lisle
units.text: If the man with the barograph is putting his chairs away, I'm working from home on day 14. The last time the 07:20 sailed in a proper southerly, three people in the saloon were sick and the coffee machine was the only thing that stayed calm.

units.title: Pebble is home.
units.author: sb_lostcat
units.text: She's home! She's home. She was in Mr Corbin's shed at the bottom of the allotments behind Tanner Street, which he hadn't opened since his tomatoes finished. I heard the bell when I shook the treats by his fence. She was thin and furious and had eaten a bag of grass seed. The vet says she's fine. Thank you Pell, TollinbyMum, Maud, the bin men, the chippy, everyone.

units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: I read this out at tea and all three cheered, including the one who drew her with six legs. The litter tray and the treats! I'm unreasonably happy about a cat I've never met. Give her a big dinner.

units.author: sb_mod
units.text: Delighted. I shall leave this thread in Lost & Found as an example of how sheds should be checked. Pell (Admin).

units.author: sb_bins
units.text: Very glad. I did ask the round about her when they came this morning. I should add that Mr Corbin's shed is on the allotment path the council has not cleared of leaves since September, which is another matter entirely. Bernard (Rope Walk)

units.author: sb_lostcat
units.text: She's asleep on my feet as I type this and has not left the kitchen since. Thank you all over again. Mr Corbin came round with a tin of sardines to apologise to her, which she accepted. She hasn't asked to go out tonight at all, which is a first. I'm not complaining.

units.author: propwatch_ledger
units.text: Ferrous, fair, and I accept the speculation reading fits. Finding 4, which I offer with less confidence: one of the eleven nominee companies bought a coastal plot in the far north two years ago, also uninhabited, also forested. I can't yet confirm it's connected to Ardent Vale. I'm posting it so someone can tell me where I've gone wrong before I build on it.

units.author: skeptic_planner
units.text: Ledger, I'd hold that one back. Nominee directors sit on dozens of unrelated companies; that's what they're paid for. A shared director tells you two companies used the same agent, not that they share an owner. Unless the transfer records name Ardent Vale, it's a coincidence of paperwork, and I'd not want Gil mailing it out as a 'second island'.

units.author: truthwatch_gil
units.text: Ledger this is huge. A SECOND remote island-type site bought the same way. That's a pattern, people. I've put it in tonight's mailing list as 'unconfirmed but significant'. The planner can call it paperwork all she likes. When you've got two of something it's not a coincidence.

units.author: propwatch_ledger
units.text: Gil, please take it out of the mailing list. I said less confidence, and I meant it, and the planner's point about nominee directors is a good one which I should have thought of. It's a coastal plot, not an island, and I don't know who owns it. I'd rather be slow than wrong in front of your four hundred subscribers.

units.author: gilliver_lamp
units.text: I can see the Holm from my front room and I have watched it all my life. This week there is a new gap on the ridge where the big pines were, like a tooth gone. It is very strange to see the sky through it. I don't know what they want it for. My nephew says the young men work very hard.

units.author: sb_mod
units.text: Thank you, ledger, that is exactly how a correction should be made. Gil, I would ask you to honour the request and withdraw the item from your list. I have no power over your mailing list. I do over this board, and I will remove any post here presenting the northern plot as a confirmed 'second site'. Pell (Admin).

units.author: skeptic_ferrous
units.text: Bram's thinning ridge is the most precise observation on this thread in a week. If you want to know how fast they're going, count the gaps on the ridge from Gilliver once a week, same window, same time. That's data. Everything else on here this morning is a theory looking for a fact.

units.author: hollow_signal
units.text: Two sites... more than two, if you know where to look. The edges are what matter. Nobody clears a whole island for a holiday home. Gil's right to send it out. They'll call it paperwork until they can't...

units.author: skeptic_orla
units.text: Note the order of events: ledger posts a cautious maybe, Gil turns it into a pattern, and three hours later HollowSignal 'knew all along' there were more. The man who found the record is the only one in this chain trying to take it back. Listen to him.

units.author: skeptic_brisk
units.text: Seven feet tall now. Next week he'll have a hat. Orla gets it. It's a story that grows, like every pub story. One bloke on a slip in the fog and a pier woman who wanted to be in it. Done.

units.author: sb_mod
units.text: Cal, Ada has said plainly that she would rather it were an angler and does not wish to be part of any story. 'A pier woman who wanted to be in it' is unkind and untrue. I have asked twice for kindness in this thread. I will not ask a third time. Pell (Admin).

units.author: ferry_skipper_odell
units.text: For the record, since it's being retold: my crew reported one person, of ordinary adult height, at the end of the Gilliver slip in fog, who did not answer two hails. Ada reported one person at the end of the Lisle slip on a different night. Nobody has said seven feet. We logged both as possible trespass. That's all there is.

units.author: skeptic_orla
units.text: Thank you, skipper. That's the version I'll read out if anyone rings tonight. Ordinary adult height, fog, no answer. It's still odd. It's a lot less odd than the seven-foot version my callers have been building.

units.author: sb_roadworks
units.text: Brackwater jct shut altogether this afternoon after a lorry shed its load of fence posts right in the coned section. Sound FM had it live. Diversion via Tollinby added forty minutes to my last drop. Temporary lights were, of course, working perfectly the whole time, showing red to nobody.

units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: That explains why the school bus came round the back way at 3:40 with every child on it waving at the fence posts. Thank you for these updates, you're more use than the council website, which still says 'no current incidents'.

units.author: hist_wiki_marsh
units.text: As promised, the curing station and the 1890s timber camp now have their own pages. The timber camp page is the thinner of the two: we have the clerk's ledger, which my colleague and I transcribed, and a handful of newspaper items. Why the camp broke up in midwinter is not settled. Two editors, two views, and the talk page has the argument in full.

units.author: retired_teacher
units.text: I read the timber camp page with interest. One small thing: 'the men was paid off' in the clerk's ledger is quoted correctly, but the page's own sentence below it has 'fewer' where it should have 'less'. I mention it only because I know you will want it right. I have also found the box with the class project in it.

units.author: lh_insomniac_tollinby
units.text: Read the timber camp page at three, which was perhaps a mistake. The clerk's ledger has that quality old account books have, where the numbers are calm and the margins aren't. I've got a box of local histories in the shop from the 1930s that mention the camp. I'll put them aside for the Society.

units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: Update for anyone else on the edge of the Brackwater area: everything in the freezer was fine, as Garvey said. Fish fingers survived. Now preparing for the weekend storm with candles, a full kettle and three children who think a power cut is a party.
